items.name: SEO
items.summary: Track your keyword rankings and competitors.
items.description: Track where your sites rank for the keywords you choose, per device and country, and follow your competitors' positions. Search results come from the search APIs you add a key for (Serper, SerpApi and seven others). Connect Google Search Console with a read-only Google sign-in. Gives your agents SEO tools when you allow them.
permissions: Sends the keywords you track to the search APIs you add a key for
Reads the search API keys you save in Girru's credentials
Connects Google Search Console with read-only access, only when you choose to
Keeps your sites, keywords and rankings in its own tables
Adds SEO tools that agents can use once you allow them

items.name: Server Monitor
items.summary: Preview: a dashboard for your servers, with sample data.
items.description: A preview of a monitoring dashboard for WHM/cPanel, Linux, AWS S3 and SSH servers: load, disk, accounts, services, SSL, email, backups, DNS, uptime and more. Today every figure is sample data. It does not connect to any server, and the server entries you save are kept in memory only, until Girru restarts. Saved passwords and tokens are never sent back to the page.
permissions: Shows sample monitoring data; makes no connection to any server
Keeps the server entries you save in memory only, until Girru restarts
Has no tables, no agent tools and no background jobs

items.name: Slack
items.summary: Preview: receive Slack messages in Girru and keep a log.
items.description: A first step for Slack in Girru. It receives the messages your Slack app sends to Girru's address, only when Slack signed them with your signing secret, and keeps them in a log you can read. Your agents can log a message for a Slack channel, but sending to Slack itself is not built yet: nothing leaves Girru. It does not answer messages by itself.
permissions: Opens one public address (/api/ext/slack/webhook) that accepts only requests Slack signed with your signing secret
Keeps the Slack settings you save; the tokens are never sent back to the page
Keeps the messages it receives and logs in its own tables
Sends nothing to Slack or anywhere else yet
Adds a slack_send tool (it logs only) that agents can use once you allow them

items.name: Terminal
items.summary: Your shell next to your agents.
items.description: A terminal inside Girru for the owner, next to the chats and the task board. Agents never get it by adding the app.
permissions: Runs commands you type, on this computer, as you

items.name: Trading
items.summary: Practice trading with an agent team.
items.description: Practice trading with fictional money and an agent team: watch the market, test ideas on past charts and see what your agents would do. No real orders are sent.
permissions: Reads market data
Practice only: never sends real orders

items.name: WAF Security
items.summary: Test how a website's firewall handles common attacks.
items.description: Sends a set of harmless test requests that look like common attacks (SQL injection, cross-site scripting, path traversal and eight more groups) to a website you name, and shows which ones its firewall (WAF) blocked and which got through. It also tries to tell which firewall the site uses. Campaigns repeat the test in four stages, now or on a daily, weekly or monthly schedule, and compare each run with the one before. A self-audit checks this Girru's own security headers, sign-in protection and rate limits. Only test sites you own or may test.
permissions: Sends attack-like test requests to the websites you enter, when you start a scan or a campaign runs
Refuses local and private network addresses unless you allow them in its settings
Runs your scheduled campaigns in the background, checked once an hour
Sends requests to this Girru's own address when you run a self-audit
Keeps scans, campaigns and its test library in its own tables
Adds a waf_scan tool that agents can use once you allow them
